algorithms.title: Next Greater Element I & II (NGE)
algorithms.summary: Find the first element to the right that is strictly greater than the current element (Linear & Circular Array).
explanation: Monotonic Decreasing Stack Strategy: Maintain a stack storing element values/indices in strictly decreasing order.
Algorithm for Linear Array: Traverse array right-to-left (or left-to-right).
1) While stack is not empty and `stack.top() <= curr_val`: Pop element from stack.
2) If stack is empty: NGE is `-1`. Else: NGE is `stack.top()`.
3) Push `curr_val` onto stack.
Circular Array Variant (NGE II): Simulate 2N iterations using index `i % N` so elements can wrap around to find next greater.

traceSteps: Step 1: Traverse right-to-left starting at 8. Stack = []. NGE[8] = -1. Push 8. Stack=[8].
Step 2: Element 10. Pop 8 (10 >= 8). Stack empty. NGE[10] = -1. Push 10. Stack=[10].
Step 3: Element 2. Stack top (10) > 2. NGE[2] = 10. Push 2. Stack=[10, 2].
Step 4: Element 5. Pop 2 (5 >= 2). Stack top (10) > 5. NGE[5] = 10. Push 5. Stack=[10, 5].
Step 5: Element 4. Stack top (5) > 4. NGE[4] = 5. Push 4. Stack=[10, 5, 4].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds nearest greater element to the right in linear O(N) single pass.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding next larger value or nearest right-side peak boundary.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Stock span calculation, temperature rise forecasting, histogram bounds.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Each element is pushed and popped at most once, yielding O(N) time.

algorithms.title: Next Smaller Element (NSE)
algorithms.summary: Find the first element to the right that is strictly smaller than the current element.
explanation: Monotonic Increasing Stack Strategy: Maintain a stack storing elements in strictly increasing order.
Traverse array right-to-left:
1) While stack is not empty and `stack.top() >= curr_val`: Pop element from stack.
2) If stack is empty: NSE is `-1`. Else: NSE is `stack.top()`.
3) Push `curr_val` onto stack.

traceSteps: Step 1: i=4 (val 25): Stack=[]. NSE = -1. Push 25.
Step 2: i=3 (val 2): Pop 25 (25 >= 2). Stack empty. NSE = -1. Push 2.
Step 3: i=2 (val 5): Stack top 2 < 5. NSE = 2. Push 5.
Step 4: i=1 (val 8): Stack top 5 < 8. NSE = 5. Push 8.
Step 5: i=0 (val 4): Pop 8 and 5 (>= 4). Stack top 2 < 4. NSE = 2.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds nearest smaller element to the right in O(N) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When determining right boundary for histogram rectangles.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Histogram area computation, minimum range boundaries.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) linear time Monotonic Stack.

2) If stack is empty: PSE is `-1`. Else: PSE is `stack.top()`.

Step 2: i=1 (val 5): Stack top 4 < 5. PSE = 4. Push 5.
Step 3: i=2 (val 2): Pop 5 and 4 (>= 2). Stack empty. PSE = -1. Push 2.

algorithms.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
algorithms.summary: Find area of largest rectangle that can be formed within a histogram of bar heights using Monotonic Stack boundaries.
explanation: Histogram Boundary Formula: For each bar at index `i` with height `h = heights[i]`, the max rectangular width it can span is `width = right_bound - left_bound - 1`.
`left_bound` = index of Previous Smaller Element (PSE).
`right_bound` = index of Next Smaller Element (NSE).

Single-Pass Stack Approach: Maintain monotonic increasing stack of indices. When popping element `tp` because `heights[i] < heights[tp]`, `heights[tp]` is the bar height, `i` is right_bound, and `stack.top()` is left_bound!

traceSteps: Step 1: i=0 (h=2): Push 0. Stack=[0].
Step 2: i=1 (h=1 < 2): Pop 0. height=2, width=1 (1 - 0). Area = 2. Push 1. Stack=[1].
Step 5: Pop 2 (h=5, width = 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 -> Area = 10!). Push 4.
Step 6: Max Area = 10.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximal contiguous rectangular area under non-uniform bar heights.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding maximum contiguous bounding rectangle in 1D/2D bar charts.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Maximum 2D matrix rectangle search, image bounding box algorithms.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Single pass O(N) time using Monotonic Stack.

codeTemplates.code:
def largestRectangleArea(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    stack = [] # Stores indices
    max_area = 0
    heights.append(0) # Sentinel
    for i, h in enumerate(heights):
        while stack and heights[stack[-1]] > h:
            height = heights[stack.pop()]
            width = i if not stack else (i - stack[-1] - 1)
            max_area = max(max_area, height * width)
        stack.append(i)
    heights.pop()
    return max_area

algorithms.title: Sliding Window Maximum (Monotonic Deque)
algorithms.summary: Find the maximum element in every sliding window of size K as it moves from left to right across array.
explanation: Monotonic Decreasing Deque Strategy: Maintain a Double-Ended Queue (Deque) storing array indices such that corresponding values `nums[idx]` are in strictly decreasing order.
Algorithm for each index `i`:
1) Out of Window Eviction: If `deque.front() <= i - K`, pop front of deque.
2) Monotonic Maintenance: While deque is not empty and `nums[deque.back()] <= nums[i]`, pop back of deque.
3) Push `i` to back of deque.
4) When `i >= K - 1`, record window maximum `nums[deque.front()]`.

traceSteps: Step 1: i=0 (val 1): Deque = [0].
Step 2: i=1 (val 3): Pop 0 (1 <= 3). Deque = [1].
Step 3: i=2 (val -1): Deque = [1, 2]. Window 1 result: nums[1] = 3.
Step 4: i=3 (val -3): Deque = [1, 2, 3]. Window 2 result: nums[1] = 3.
Step 5: i=4 (val 5): Pop out of window 1. Pop 2, 3 (<= 5). Deque = [4]. Window 3 result: nums[4] = 5.
Step 6: Continue for all windows -> Output = [3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes rolling maximum in sliding window of size K in O(N) total time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding maximum or minimum in fixed sliding time windows.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Real-time stock price peak monitor, network packet latency max burst filter.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Deque elements are pushed/popped at most once, reducing O(N*K) naive loop to O(N).

algorithms.title: Min-Heap & Max-Heap Implementation & Heapify
algorithms.summary: Master Priority Queue Min-Heap and Max-Heap binary tree array implementations with O(N) heapify and O(log N) shiftUp/shiftDown operations.
explanation: Complete Binary Tree Array Mapping: For node at index `i`, parent is `(i - 1) // 2`, left child is `2*i + 1`, right child is `2*i + 2`.
Min-Heap Invariant: `heap[parent] <= heap[child]`.
`shiftUp(i)`: Swap element at index `i` with its parent while `heap[i] < heap[parent]`.
`shiftDown(i)`: Swap element at index `i` with its smallest child while `heap[i] > min(children)`.
O(N) Heapify: Build heap from array bottom-up starting from first non-leaf node `(N//2 - 1)` down to 0.

traceSteps: Step 1: Insert 5 -> Heap=[5].
Step 2: Insert 3 -> shiftUp(1) swaps 3 and 5 -> Heap=[3, 5].
Step 3: Insert 8 -> Heap=[3, 5, 8].
Step 4: Insert 1 -> shiftUp(3) swaps 1 & 5, then 1 & 3 -> Heap=[1, 3, 8, 5].
Step 5: Insert 2 -> shiftUp(4) swaps 2 & 3 -> Heap=[1, 2, 8, 5, 3].
Step 6: Root element is min = 1.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Maintains dynamically updated minimum/maximum priority element in logarithmic time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When repeatedly fetching highest/lowest priority item from streaming data.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Dijkstra shortest path algorithm, OS process scheduler, Huffman coding tree.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(1) minimum retrieval with O(log N) insertion/deletion.

algorithms.title: Find Median from Data Stream (Two Heaps Pattern)
algorithms.summary: Continuously compute the median of a streaming sequence of numbers using a Max-Heap for lower half and Min-Heap for upper half.
explanation: Two Heaps Architecture:
1) `max_heap` (Lower Half): Stores smaller half of numbers, root is maximum of lower half.
2) `min_heap` (Upper Half): Stores larger half of numbers, root is minimum of upper half.
Invariants: `max_heap.size()` is either equal to or 1 greater than `min_heap.size()`, and every element in `max_heap` is $\le$ every element in `min_heap`.
Finding Median: If `len(max_heap) > len(min_heap)`, median is `max_heap.top()`. Else, median is `(max_heap.top() + min_heap.top()) / 2.0`.

traceSteps: Step 1: Add 1 -> max_heap=[1], min_heap=[]. Median = 1.0.
Step 2: Add 2 -> max_heap=[1], min_heap=[2]. Median = (1 + 2)/2 = 1.5.
Step 3: Add 3 -> max_heap=[2, 1], min_heap=[3]. Median = max_heap.top() = 2.0.
Step 4: All stream medians computed in O(1) time per query.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes continuous median of an unbounded incoming data stream in real-time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding running median of dynamic streaming data.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Real-time latency median monitoring, financial tick stream median price calculation.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Two Heaps maintain equal halves in O(log N) insert time with O(1) median query.

algorithms.title: Trapping Rain Water (Monotonic Stack & Two Pointers)
algorithms.summary: Calculate total trapped rainwater between elevation bars using Two Pointers or Monotonic Stack boundaries.
explanation: Water Trapping Condition: Water trapped at index `i` is `min(left_max, right_max) - height[i]`.
Two Pointers Strategy (O(1) Space): Maintain `left` and `right` pointers, along with `left_max` and `right_max`.
If `height[left] <= height[right]`: If `height[left] >= left_max`, update `left_max`; else add `left_max - height[left]` to total water. Move `left++`.
Else (`height[left] > height[right]`): If `height[right] >= right_max`, update `right_max`; else add `right_max - height[right]` to total water. Move `right--`.

traceSteps: Step 1: Pointers left=0 (h=0), right=11 (h=1). left_max=0, right_max=1.
Step 2: Trapped water accumulates at indices 2 (1 unit), 4 (1 unit), 5 (2 units), 6 (1 unit), 9 (1 unit).
Step 3: Total Trapped Water = 6 units.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes total bounded liquid capacity between 2D terrain elevation bars.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When computing volume of trapped liquid or bounded valley capacity.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Geographic terrain water accumulation modeling, 2D container fluid capacity.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) single pass with O(1) two-pointer memory.

codeTemplates.code:
def trap(height: list[int]) -> int:
    if not height: return 0
    l, r = 0, len(height) - 1
    left_max, right_max = height[l], height[r]
    water = 0
    while l < r:
        if left_max <= right_max:
            l += 1
            left_max = max(left_max, height[l])
            water += left_max - height[l]
        else:
            r -= 1
            right_max = max(right_max, height[r])
            water += right_max - height[r]
    return water

algorithms.title: Min Stack (O(1) GetMin Design)
algorithms.summary: Design a Stack supporting push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in O(1) constant time.
explanation: Auxiliary Min Stack Strategy: Maintain two stacks: primary `stack` and `min_stack`.
Push `x`: Push `x` to `stack`. Push `min(x, min_stack.top())` to `min_stack`.
Pop: Pop from both `stack` and `min_stack`.
GetMin: Return `min_stack.top()` in $O(1)$ time.

exampleTrace.input: Push -2, Push 0, Push -3, GetMin, Pop, Top, GetMin
traceSteps: Step 1: Push -2 -> stack=[-2], min_stack=[-2].
Step 2: Push 0 -> stack=[-2, 0], min_stack=[-2, -2].
Step 3: Push -3 -> stack=[-2, 0, -3], min_stack=[-2, -2, -3].
Step 4: GetMin -> returns min_stack.top() = -3.
Step 5: Pop -> stack=[-2, 0], min_stack=[-2, -2].
Step 6: Top = 0, GetMin = -2.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Provides constant-time O(1) minimum retrieval for stack structures.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When tracking running minimum of stack history.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Undo-redo buffer with min state, tracking lowest temperature reading.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(1) constant time for push, pop, top, and getMin.

algorithms.title: Top K Frequent Elements
algorithms.summary: Find the K most frequent elements in an array using Frequency Map and Min-Heap of size K.
explanation: Min-Heap of Size K Strategy:
Step 1: Count frequency of each element using HashMap `count_map`.
Step 2: Maintain a Min-Heap ordered by frequency storing `(freq, element)` pairs.
Step 3: Push elements to Min-Heap. If `heap.size() > K`, pop the root (evicts element with smallest frequency).
Step 4: Remaining K elements in Min-Heap are the top K most frequent elements!

traceSteps: Step 1: Frequency map: {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 1}.
Step 2: Insert (3, 1) -> Min-Heap = [(3, 1)].
Step 3: Insert (2, 2) -> Min-Heap = [(2, 2), (3, 1)].
Step 4: Insert (1, 3) -> Heap size 3 > 2! Pop root (1, 3). Min-Heap remains [(2, 2), (3, 1)].
Step 5: Output elements: [1, 2].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Extracts the top K highest frequency elements from dynamic streaming data.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding most frequent items under memory bound K.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Trending hashtag monitor, search term frequency ranking.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N log K) time using Min-Heap of size K.
